title: Why You Should Never, Ever Gossip About Students udents/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin distinguishes professional consultation about difficult students from gossip—criticism not respectfully intended for a student's benefit—and argues gossip damages both teacher and classroom even when it feels harmless. He explains that venting negatively about students solidifies negative thoughts in the teacher's mind, gradually turning them into the 'cynical, seen-it-all teacher' depicted in movies, and that this negativity is impossible to hide from students despite best efforts. Because rapport and influence depend on students sensing genuine goodwill, harboring or expressing resentment toward students undermines a teacher's ability to positively affect behavior. He closes with a call to choose forgiveness, encouragement, and daily renewal instead of participating in staff-room gossip.
points: Gossip is defined as any criticism of specific students that isn't respectfully intended for their benefit—distinct from legitimate professional consultation with colleagues.
Venting negatively about students, even in the 'safety' of the teachers' lounge, solidifies negative thoughts and sabotages hopes for the classroom.
Habitual negativity gradually turns teachers into the 'cynical, seen-it-all' archetype who sees only faults in students and school.
Negative feelings toward students are impossible to fully hide—students sense resentment or animosity and return the sentiment.
Rapport and behavioral influence depend on students not sensing denigration; choosing forgiveness and encouragement daily protects that relationship.
quotes: Before you answer no, it’s important to clarify that any criticism of particular students that isn’t respectfully intended for their benefit is gossip—no two ways about it.
But doing so puts you at a disadvantage when you step in front of your class, because every time you verbalize negative thoughts about your students, they solidify in your mind.

You’ll become one of them—the cynical, seen-it-all teacher so shamefully depicted in so many movies and TV shows, leaving no room in your heart for love, hope, and faith in the students placed under care.
If you harbor resentment, dislike, or animosity toward any one or more of your students, they’ll know it—guaranteed—and will return the sentiment.
And without a trusting, affable relationship with your students, you’ll lack the leverage you need to influence their behavior.
Choose instead to see only the best in your students. Choose to forgive and forget and wipe the slate clean at the end of every day.
